title: Fanout budgeting and graceful degradation protocol for region failover and retries
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Introduce a standards-driven policy (protocol + SDK contract) that limits cross-service fanout for hedged requests, enforces SLO-aligned retry budgets, and defines idempotency token semantics to make retries safe across multi-region failovers. This ticket drives the runtime and SDK changes needed to safely reduce cascading retries, enable graceful degradation under overload, and give teams per-route controls tied to SLO classes.
acceptance_criteria: A decision graph doc that maps request class -> fanout budget -> retry/hedge policy exists and is reviewed by SRE and API teams
SDKs (Python, Go, and JS) expose a standardized Idempotency header name and TTL behavior with backward-compatible defaults
Runtime enforces per-customer and per-route fanout budgets and emits telemetry for fanout breaches and hedge activations
Playbook for multi-region failover includes safe fallback orderings that respect fanout budgets and circuit breaker state
Feature gated rollout starts in sandboxes and no customer-facing regressions observed in first 2 weeks
decisions: Canonical idempotency header: 'X-RI-Idempotency-Token' with recommended UUIDv4 values and optional semantic suffix for dedup keys
Idempotency token TTL: default 24 hours; SDKs will allow override per-call where application demands shorter TTL
Hedged requests allowed only for SLO class 'interactive' and 'high-priority-batch' with strict per-request fanout budgets
Fanout budget model: per-request 'budget' expressed in tokens; each downstream invocation consumes 1 token; hedged retries reserve tokens atomically at router time
Circuit breakers should add a lightweight affinity tag to routing telemetry so failovers avoid saturated regions until healthy
Load-shedding first-tier: serve stale-cached prefix responses or degraded feature flags instead of retry amplification
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (runtime): implement fanout-budget enforcement in router (tokens reservation, budget accounting, and breach telemetry)
Phase 1 (SDK): add helper to generate X-RI-Idempotency-Token and attach TTL metadata; provide guidance for token persistence and collision handling
Phase 2 (runtime): integrate fanout budgets with circuit-breaker state so region fallback reserves lower budgets for fallback routes
Phase 2 (policy): publish per-route default budgets tied to SLO classes and expose overrides to product teams via Console
Phase 3 (rollout): gated rollout on a sample of customers and core internal services, collect metrics for retries, latencies, customer error rates
rollback_plan: Feature-flag the entire fanout accounting system and provide a runaway kill-switch to disable enforcement and revert to current best-effort behavior
If SDK changes cause client errors, release a patch that reverts to attaching tokens only when caller opts-in via explicit flag
Re-initialize any stuck reservation state with an admin job that clears stale holds older than token TTL
metrics_and_slos: Primary: 99th percentile p95/p99 request latency per SLO class before and after hedging
Control: retry amplification factor (total downstream calls / originating requests) should reduce by >= 30% for overloaded episodes
Safety: rate of idempotent-dedup collisions should be < 0.0001% for production traffic
Operational: fanout budget breach events per 1M requests and time-to-heal after circuit open
sdk_changes: Python/Go/JS SDKs: add method generate_idempotency_token(ttl_seconds=86400, prefix=None) and automatic header injection helper
Behavior: SDK will persist tokens in-memory per-call by default; docs will show patterns for durable storage when cross-process dedup is needed
Compatibility: SDK will not alter existing user requests unless callers explicitly enable 'safe_retry' or call client.request_with_idempotency()
Telemetry: SDKs will emit events when tokens are recycled, expired, or rejected by server-side deduplication
rollout_notes: Start with non-customer-facing internal APIs (metrics ingestion, telemetry pipelines) to validate fanout accounting
Enable on a single low-traffic region pair to validate multi-region fallback interactions before wide rollout
Coordinate with Console team to surface per-route budget overrides and a visualization for hedged calls
Prepare communications to partner teams: SSO, Billing, and Customer Success for potential transient errors during rollout
